title: DHCPFO: Improve handling of vendor-specific options
description:
This changes the DHCPFO vendor-specific option handling so that it is possible to define non-Microsoft vendor-specific options. I got an example of Infoblox DHCPFO packet with option 30 that contains DHCP client hostname, while with Microsoft the option 30 is DHCP scope ID.

Infoblox (= when Microsoft was not autodetected or configured):

```
DHCP Style Option, infoblox-client-hostname (30), "XXXXXXXX"
    Option Code: (vendor-specific) (30)
    Length: 8
    Client hostname (Infoblox-specific): XXXXXXXX
```
(display filter = `dhcpfo.infoblox.clienthostname`)

Microsoft (in Update request packet):

```
DHCP Style Option, microsoft-scope-ID (30)
    Option Code: (vendor-specific) (30)
    Length: 4
    DHCP scope ID (Microsoft-specific): 10.1.2.32
```
(display filter = `dhcpfo.microsoft.scopeid`)

Also changed all the vendor-specific options' display filter field names to `dhcpfo.<vendor>.<optionname>` (instead of `dhcpfo.ms<optionname>`).

Note: The previous DHCPFO code/behaviour (that is changed by this MR) was not yet cherry-picked to 4.0 (or 3.6), so these field changes are not disruptive to Wireshark release users.

For unknown options this also shows the data bytes in the tree for easier access:

```
    DHCP Style Option, Unknown Option (36)
        Option Code: Unknown (36)
        Length: 1
        Unknown data: 01
    DHCP Style Option, Unknown Option (38)
        Option Code: Unknown (38)
        Length: 4
        Unknown data: 00000000
    DHCP Style Option, Unknown Option (39)
        Option Code: Unknown (39)
        Length: 1
        Unknown data: 00
```
